subject: maths-aa-sl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: The quadratic function

points.text: Standard form: y-intercept and axis of symmetry
Vertex form: vertex and completing the square

bigPicture: Every quadratic can be written three ways, and each form shows something different: the y-intercept, the roots, or the vertex.

keyIdeas.cue: What does ax² + bx + c show directly?
keyIdeas.answer: y-intercept (0, c); axis x = −b/(2a); opens up if a > 0.

keyIdeas.cue: What does a(x − p)(x − q) show?
What does a(x − h)² + k show?
keyIdeas.answer: Vertex (h, k); found by completing the square.

misconceptions.right: It is (−2, −5): sign flips inside the bracket.

misconceptions.wrong: Forgetting to multiply the −9 by a

practice.prompt: f(x) = x² − 4x − 5. (a) Factorise. (b) Write in vertex form. (c) State the range.
A ball's height is h = −4.9t² + 14t + 1.5. Find the maximum height and when it occurs.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: Factorised form and vertex form and what each reveals
formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers.
